subject: E-Commerce
title: Anchoring: The First Number Wins
description: A quick, practical guide to Anchoring: The First Number Wins.

hook.text: Show someone $500 first, then $200, and $200 feels cheap. The first number anchors all future judgments.

buildup.text: E-commerce uses anchoring everywhere: 'Was $120, now $59!' The original price sets the mental reference.

discovery.text: JCPenney removed fake sales and showed honest prices. Revenue dropped 25%. Shoppers missed the anchor.

twist.text: Amazon shows 'list price' crossed out next to a lower selling price. The list price is often inflated.

climax.text: Anchoring means no price exists in isolation. Every price is judged relative to the first one you see.

punchline.text: JCPenney tried honest pricing and lost 25%. Shoppers need anchors to feel smart.

quiz.question: What happened when JCPenney removed fake sales and showed honest prices?
